text:
For a renter, I’d choose the **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W panel kit**. It’s a self-contained setup: the panel charges the battery, and you plug devices into the power station—no permanent wiring or connection to the apartment’s electrical system. The kit is listed at **$489.99**; [see the kit and current price](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2-100w-solar-kit). ([Product details](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-for-an-apartment-balcony))

Its **288 Wh battery** is suited to phones, a laptop, a router, or a fan—not a refrigerator. If fridge backup is your goal, look at a much larger station; a guide lists the **Anker SOLIX C800X** as a balcony-recharging option with 960 Wh capacity, though you’d need to check the matching panel and kit details. ([Apartment power-station guide](https://powerbencher.com/stories/home-backup/best-portable-power-stations-apartment/))

Before setting up a panel, check your lease and building rules, and make sure it can’t fall or catch wind. A portable panel-and-battery setup is different from a plug-in balcony solar system, which feeds power into the apartment wiring. ([Balcony-kit guide](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-for-an-apartment-balcony))

judge.top_pick: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel Kit
